solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Difficult to control rising feeling of sympathy

parts.note: rising means going up, so it gives the word up
pity is a feeling of sympathy for another's suffering

explanation.surface: Someone describes a surge of compassion that is hard to keep in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like it describes the feeling, but it simply supplies UP, placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone self-important and unruly is hard to keep under control.

clue.text: As part of a square, 'i' may be not authentic

definitions.text: As part of a square, 'i' may be
definitions.meaning: in mathematics i is the square root of minus one, an imaginary number, so it is not a real number

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is mathematical: i, whose square is minus one, is an imaginary number rather than a real one.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean lacking reality: an imaginary number in maths and something fake in everyday speech.

clue.text: Translator brought in during shake-up, manipulated puppet

indicators.note: brought in during means placed inside the letters of the following words
manipulated means handled and rearranged, so the combined letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An interpreter is drafted in amid a reorganisation, and a puppet is worked by strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' is both the anagram signal and a fitting word for working a puppet, so the surface and the mechanism share it.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Petrushka is the Russian puppet hero of Stravinsky's ballet, a figure of folk puppet shows.

clue.text: Return of oral rent in big city

indicators.note: return means coming back, so the two words that follow are read backwards

parts.note: a viva (viva voce) is an oral examination
to let is to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A demand to pay back rent that was agreed only by word of mouth in a large city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' reverses VIVALET as a whole, giving the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Israel's second city, a large coastal metropolis on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: One measures the distance when Bible Queen circumnavigates Millennium building

indicators.note: circumnavigates means sails right round, so the first letters go around the building

parts.note: OT, the Old Testament, stands for part of the Bible
the Millennium Dome is the London building put up for the year 2000
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: A journey is clocked when a biblical queen sails around a famous building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome is the large tent-like building in Greenwich, London, put up to mark the year 2000; 'Bible Queen' looks like one person but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the instrument in a vehicle that records the distance travelled.

clue.text: Logically peculiar manner of speaking to supporter

parts.note: a dialect is a form of speech peculiar to a region or group
an ally is someone who backs you up

explanation.surface: A curious way of talking, explained by reasoning, is offered to a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' simply joins the two pieces; the definition leans on the sense of dialectic, the art of logical argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare sense: dialectal can mean relating to dialectic, the method of logical disputation, so this adverb means by reasoned argument.

clue.text: Aims of criminal, one or several

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of the two words are bent out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question about the goals of a crook, whether there is one of them or a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges AIMSOF, then I follows. The definition takes 'several' as several members of the Sicilian crime organisation, the word being plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the plural form, naming several members of the Mafia rather than a single one.

clue.text: Holy time of intercession?

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the answer lies within the next word

explanation.surface: A question whether a sacred hour is when prayers on others' behalf are said.
explanation.definitionFit: Terce is one of the canonical hours of prayer, the third hour, around nine in the morning.

clue.text: Heartlessly opposing being moved

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: opposing means fighting against, resisting

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly resists being shifted somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes the middle S of the nine-letter RESISTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing something somewhere else, moving it to a new location, is relocating it.

clue.text: Noise made by conductor

definitions.meaning: a clattering sound, such as loose objects shaken together
Sir Simon ... is a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A racket kicked up by the person on the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Simon Rattle is the British conductor of, among others, the Berlin Philharmonic and London Symphony orchestras.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a clattering sound; the other is the surname of a famous orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Calls to attention of enthusiasts about cost of transport

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: fans are enthusiasts
a fare is the price paid for a journey

explanation.surface: Supporters are urged to notice what travel costs.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: trumpet flourishes that announce someone and demand people's notice.

clue.text: Strong drink advanced in the capacity of lunch, maybe coming back around six

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
qua is Latin for in the role or capacity of
VI is the Roman numeral six

indicators.note: coming back means the word for having lunch is read backwards

parts.note: lunch is an example of what you eat

explanation.surface: A stiff drink taken as lunch, coming back again at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is used loosely: the reversed meal sits next to the numeral rather than wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for water of life, a term for strong spirits such as brandy or schnapps.

clue.text: Nails to fasten cloth will be OK mixed with ten others

indicators.note: mixed with means the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction that combining a couple of letters with ten further items will be fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed with' rearranges OK plus TENOTHERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are hooked nails on a frame that held cloth stretched while it dried, the source of the idiom about suspense.

clue.text: Nothing green to be seen

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: No greenery is visible anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly is plain to view, not hidden away.

clue.text: Be without plans to be naked

definitions.meaning: to have a free diary, with no engagements arranged
to wear no clothes at all

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase means an empty schedule and an unclothed body.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom covers both an empty diary and wearing no clothes, two senses of lacking anything arranged or put on.

clue.text: Rotating bodies sounding like bank figures

indicators.note: sounding like means the answer is said the same as the phrase that follows

parts.note: giro stats: Giro was the British banking and payment system, and stats are figures

explanation.surface: Spinning things that come across like a bank's numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: Girobank was a British bank run through post offices, so its statistics would be giro stats.
explanation.definitionFit: These are devices built around a spinning wheel that keep their orientation, so rotating bodies describes them.

clue.text: Slaves in trouble about damaged silks

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

indicators.note: damaged means spoiled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Captives get into difficulty over spoiled fine fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ADO to ODA, and 'damaged' rearranges SILKS to LISKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Odalisques were female slaves or concubines in a Turkish harem.

clue.text: Refrain from mentioning Dave hugging naked single girlfriend

indicators.note: hugging means wrapping round, so the name goes around the word for naked

parts.note: raw can mean bare or naked
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single
a lover is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about Dave embracing an unclothed lone girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to avoid discussing something embarrassing, as if covering it with cloth.

clue.text: Broadcast notice about male idiot

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
he is a male pronoun
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A broadcast announcement concerning a foolish man.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a slang term for a stupid person, as if the skull were empty.

clue.text: Succession of turns in French department that is touristy at both ends

parts.note: Var is a department of southern France
ie, id est, means that is

indicators.note: at both ends means taking the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sequence of excursions in a French region, which is a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succession of turns' is a show of successive acts, a theatrical sense of turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety show is a series of separate acts or turns by different performers.

clue.text: Old boy repelled by tweet — youngsters may find it fun

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a peep is a small bird's chirp

explanation.surface: A former pupil is put off by a social media post that children enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns OB round; the definition is the game peekaboo, not the nursery rhyme shepherdess.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the peekaboo game played with babies, hiding and reappearing for amusement.

clue.text: It concentrates light in Lebanese cedar regularly

indicators.note: regularly means picking letters at fixed intervals, here every third

explanation.surface: Something focusing sunlight found in a cedar tree from Lebanon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes every third letter, starting with the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A device emitting an intense narrow beam of coherent light, so it focuses light.

clue.text: Monarchy's female graduate

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A kingdom's woman with a degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as is; the biblical Queen of Sheba ruled this ancient kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an ancient kingdom of southern Arabia, ruled by the queen who visited Solomon.

clue.text: Quick dance first — et voila!

indicators.note: first means the dance comes before the word for quick

parts.note: a hey or hay is an old country dance
presto is the musical term for very fast

explanation.surface: A fast dance goes first, and there you have it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations by a magician announcing a trick's sudden result.

clue.text: Stolen key not unknown possibly to be this kind

indicators.note: possibly signals a rearrangement of the letters of the two words
not signals that the letter for unknown is left out of the shuffle

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A stolen key, not unidentified, might be of a particular sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove Y from STOLENKEY and rearrange; the answer completes the phrase with 'key', a key opening many locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key, filed to open many locks, is this type, so the clue's key belongs to the sort.

clue.text: Waxed device held by busy person

indicators.note: held by means contained within the following word

parts.note: a busy bee is a hard worker
a cam is a mechanical device on a rotating shaft

explanation.surface: Something polished, a gadget gripped by a hard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waxed' suggests polishing, but it means grew, as the moon does.
explanation.definitionFit: Waxed in the sense of grew or turned into, as the moon waxes full.

clue.text: In beginning, Democratic American is romantic

indicators.note: in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: start means beginning
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
US means American

explanation.surface: From the outset, a Democrat from America is a romantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts DUS inside START; the definition is a noun, a dreamy romantic quality.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a dreamy, romantic quality or feeling, as in having stars in one's eyes.

clue.text: Herb heard noise of snake, going to work

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: a snake makes a hiss
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A herb picked up the sibilance of a snake before going off to its job.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic plant of the mint family used in cooking and herbal medicine.
